study.research_problem: Patient-specific fixation in orthognathic surgery is well studied for immediate positional accuracy, but evidence that skeletal position remains stable after healing is sparse and inconsistently imaged.
study.exact_gap: Many PSI accuracy studies lack radiographic comparison between the early postoperative state and at least 6-12 months, leaving medium- or long-term skeletal stability uncertain (S002:C01-S002:C02).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Systematically evaluate PSI skeletal stability after orthognathic surgery, with secondary assessment of operative time, complications, and reoperations, using conventional plates as controls where available and single-arm studies for qualitative synthesis (S003:C01-S004:C01).
study.study_design: PRISMA-2020 systematic review registered on OSF; five databases plus reference searching yielded six human studies and 171 participants, with ROBINS-I v2 for five studies and RoB 2 for one randomized trial (S003:C01; S005:C01-S010:C01).
study.sample_or_model: Four retrospective cohorts and two prospective studies (one multicenter RCT), with 12-53 patients per study, maxillary and/or mandibular PSI fixation, different design software, CBCT/CT/lateral cephalograms, and 6- to roughly 12-month imaging in most studies (S011:C01-S011:C03).
comparators: PSI versus conventional miniplates in a subset of included studies
Single-arm PSI early-postoperative versus later-postoperative position in other studies
Indirect comparison with historical conventional-plate literature in the discussion
No common landmark, imaging modality, operation, movement magnitude, or follow-up across all studies
method_spine: Define stability as change from early postoperative to later postoperative imaging, not preoperative-to-postoperative accuracy.
Extract operation, jaw, landmark, axis, imaging modality, follow-up, PSI system, and comparator.
Report linear, angular, transverse, and rotational changes separately.
State how many studies and patients contribute to each summary.
Keep stability, operative workflow, complications, mechanical strength, and patient-important outcomes distinct.

verification: The review reports registration, databases/search dates, dual screening, third-reviewer resolution, eligibility, 2393-to-6 selection, extraction fields, and risk-of-bias tools (S003:C01-S010:C01).
Study tables make imaging modality, time points, landmarks, jaw, and software visible (S011:C01-S012:C03).
validation: Later-versus-early imaging assesses observed skeletal positional stability in included patients; it does not mechanically validate PSI strength, fatigue, interface behavior, or causal superiority.
The review performs no independent validation and includes only one randomized comparison; three studies are low, two moderate, and one serious risk of bias (S010:C01).
sensitivity: No formal sensitivity analysis tests imaging modality, landmark, jaw, movement magnitude, follow-up, single-arm versus controlled design, or risk-of-bias exclusion.
The discussion qualitatively flags 2D/3D mixing, retrospective designs, small samples, and scarcity beyond 24 months (S019:C07-S020:C01).
application_prediction: A shift toward PSI as primary fixation is proposed, but comparative adoption decisions require stronger randomized, resource, complication, and long-term evidence (S019:C04-S020:C01).

primary_outcomes: Reported maxillary translations were 0.27-0.50 mm in x, 0.30-1.07 mm in y, and 0.529-0.656 mm direct distance; one mandibular study reported 0.729 mm at point B (S012:C01-S013:C01).

Single-study angular/transverse/rotational outcomes included 0.57 degrees SNA, 0.05 degrees SNB, 0.05/0.16 mm anterior/posterior arch width, and 0.1/0.5/0.2 degrees pitch/roll/yaw (S012:C02-S016:C01).
Only one comparative study reported operation time, 5.76 versus 6.83 hours (15.7% shorter with PSI); the other five did not report it (S017:C01).
Three studies (46 participants) reported no complications or reoperations, while three studies did not report those outcomes; missing reporting cannot be interpreted as zero risk (S018:C01).
The review states that methodological heterogeneity and absence of follow-up beyond 24 months prevent a definite long-term conclusion (S020:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: A small heterogeneous clinical evidence map with one RCT and medium-term imaging stability estimates; insufficient for a robust comparative effect, long-term device reliability, complication rate, or mechanical-validation claim.

argument_map.central_claim: Available studies show small medium-term skeletal positional changes after PSI orthognathic fixation, generally within commonly cited clinical thresholds, but sparse controlled evidence, mixed imaging/landmarks, limited follow-up, and missing complication reporting support viability rather than proven superiority or long-term reliability.
data: Six studies, 171 patients, multiple jaws/procedures/software/imaging modalities and 6-12-month follow-up (S011:C01-S011:C03).
Axis- and landmark-specific positional changes, one operation-time comparison, and incomplete complication reports (S012:C01-S018:C01).
argument_map.warrant: Small early-to-later positional changes are consistent with skeletal stability, provided imaging error, landmark definition, planned movement, relapse direction, and comparator context are considered.
backing: The review compares observed movements with conventional orthognathic thresholds of less than 2 mm translation and less than 4 degrees rotation (S019:C01-S019:C02).
argument_map.qualifier: Clinically acceptable medium-term imaging stability in selected studies, not definitive long-term comparative fixation performance.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Follow-up as short as six months is labeled long term, and no study extends beyond 24 months in the review's conclusion (S011:C03; S020:C01).
CBCT/CT and lateral cephalograms, landmarks, axes, jaws, procedures, and early reference times differ, limiting comparability.
Several summary parameters come from one study; pooled weighted means for two or three studies do not overcome conceptual heterogeneity (S017:C01).
Three studies are missing complication/reoperation information, so a minimal complication probability cannot be inferred (S018:C01; S019:C06).
Only one study supplies operation time and preoperative design/manufacturing time is outside the intraoperative comparison (S017:C01; S019:C04-S019:C05).
Skeletal positional stability does not directly establish plate strength, fatigue life, osseointegration, occlusal function, PROMs, or cost-effectiveness.

measured: At review level, search/screening/risk-of-bias data and extracted study characteristics; positional changes, operation time, complications, and reoperations were measured or reported by included clinical studies (S009:C01-S018:C01).
inferred: The review interprets small positional changes relative to literature thresholds as clinically acceptable stability and indirectly as reliable fixation (S019:C01-S019:C02; S020:C01).
It theorizes that digital planning and simplified intraoperative procedures make PSI outcomes similar or better than miniplates, but this is not isolated by the included evidence (S019:C02-S019:C06).
recommended: Use standardized 3D imaging, consistent early and long-term time points, prespecified landmarks/coordinate systems, longer than 24-month follow-up, randomized comparators, complete harms, PROMs, workflow time, and cost reporting (S019:C05-S020:C01).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Millimetric or angular positional change is a skeletal stability endpoint, not a mechanical strength or fatigue test.
Position within a clinical threshold does not establish superiority over conventional fixation without a concurrent comparable control.
No reported complication in a small study is not proof of zero risk; unreported outcomes are missing, not negative.
Shorter operating time excludes planning, engineering, fabrication, transport, and approval time.
Six- to twelve-month imaging does not establish true long-term relapse, hardware failure, or patient benefit.
overclaim_risks: The abstract calls PSI reliable with a high level of long-term stability despite medium-term follow-up and mostly observational evidence (S001:C01-S001:C02).
The discussion's statement of no significant complications/reoperations conflates three zero-event reports with three non-reporting studies (S019:C01; S018:C01).
Indirect historical comparisons and common thresholds cannot demonstrate PSI superiority (S019:C02).
The automatic experimental-mechanical and animal cues are false; this article is a clinical systematic review.

section_moves.move: Separate immediate accuracy from longitudinal stability
section_moves.execution: The paper defines the gap as absence of later radiography comparing early and longer-term postoperative position, despite abundant immediate accuracy studies (S002:C01-S002:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For patient-specific devices, distinguish design accuracy, postoperative placement accuracy, temporal stability, mechanical durability, and clinical effectiveness as separate questions.
section_moves.failure_mode: A device can be placed accurately yet relapse or fail later, and stability can be acceptable without proving superior clinical outcomes.

section_moves.move: Attach every geometric estimate to its evidence denominator and measurement definition
section_moves.execution: The tables identify jaw, landmark, axis, imaging time frame, study count, patient count, estimate, variability, and range (S012:C01-S017:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Report geometric synthesis as parameter, coordinate/landmark, modality, early reference, follow-up, number of studies/patients, estimate, uncertainty, and comparability caveat.
section_moves.failure_mode: A weighted mean across differently defined coordinates is descriptive, not necessarily a valid pooled effect.

section_moves.execution: Three studies report no complications/reoperations, and three provide no information (S018:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Use separate counts for zero events, not assessed, and not reported; never combine them into a low-risk statement.
section_moves.failure_mode: No report is not evidence of no event.

section_moves.move: Balance intraoperative savings against upstream digital workflow
section_moves.execution: The discussion places a single 15.7% operation-time estimate beside planning/design durations and reported fabrication/delivery delays (S019:C04-S019:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Evaluate patient-specific workflows from imaging acquisition through delivery, not only incision-to-closure time.
section_moves.failure_mode: An intraoperative time gain may coexist with greater total latency and labor.

section_moves.move: State a viability conclusion while admitting the long-term evidence gate is unmet
section_moves.execution: The conclusion says a definite long-term conclusion is unavailable but describes medium-to-long-term stability as clinically acceptable and PSI as viable (S020:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: When long-term evidence is absent, use 'medium-term imaging stability supports viability' and state the precise follow-up and design needed before reliability or superiority claims.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not use 'proved' or 'reliable' after acknowledging that the decisive evidence is missing.

author_reported: Few eligible studies, mixed 2D/3D radiography, mostly retrospective cohorts, potential confounding, small samples, and no robust follow-up beyond 24 months (S019:C07-S020:C01).
reader_identified: Single-arm and controlled studies are mixed, and only one included study is randomized.
Coordinate systems, landmarks, jaws, operations, movement magnitudes, imaging modalities, early reference times, and follow-up differ.
Descriptive weighted means may imply more homogeneity than exists and are not comparative treatment effects.
No formal meta-analysis, heterogeneity statistic, sensitivity analysis, certainty grading, or publication-bias assessment.
Operation time comes from one study and complications are unreported in half of the studies.
No mechanical strength/fatigue, PROM, occlusal-function, quality-of-life, or cost-effectiveness synthesis.
Six months is insufficient to justify an unqualified 'long-term' label.
likely_bias_direction: Positive digital-surgery framing and indirect historical comparison likely overstate comparative benefit.
Small selected cohorts and incomplete harms reporting likely underestimate complications and reoperations.
Pooling small positional values across heterogeneous definitions may create false precision.
limitations.scope_boundary: The review supports selected PSI systems as showing small medium-term postoperative positional changes; it does not prove long-term mechanical reliability, lower complication risk, superior clinical outcomes, or broad superiority over conventional miniplates.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate patient-specific implant accuracy, temporal skeletal stability, mechanical durability, and clinical effectiveness into distinct research questions and claims.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Introduction gap, endpoint taxonomy, Results, and conclusion boundary.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Small positional change at 6-12 months is neither fatigue validation nor proof of better patient outcomes.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Synthesize geometric stability only after preserving coordinate, landmark, modality, early reference, follow-up, and denominator.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Systematic-review extraction table and quantitative summary.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A pooled weighted mean is not interpretable if studies measure different anatomical constructs.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Distinguish zero-event, not-assessed, and not-reported harms and couple operating-room time with full digital-workflow latency.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Safety table, workflow Results, and translational Discussion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Three missing safety reports do not support a low complication rate, and shorter surgery does not imply shorter total care time.

critical_weaknesses: Only six heterogeneous studies and one randomized comparison.
Medium-term follow-up, mixed imaging/landmarks, and descriptive rather than causal synthesis.
Half the studies do not report harms and operation time comes from one study.

summary_zh: 这是一篇正颌 PSI 临床影像稳定性的系统综述，而不是力学实验。6 项研究共 171 人，只有 1 项多中心 RCT；多数随访为 6–12 个月，且 CBCT、CT、侧位头影、坐标、标志点和手术类型不统一。观察到的位移/角度多在常用临床阈值内，因此可写成‘中期影像稳定性支持可行性’，但还不能写成长期机械可靠或优于常规钢板。手术时间缩短 15.7% 只来自 1 项研究，而且应与术前规划、设计、制造和运输时长同报。3 项研究报告零并发症，另 3 项完全未报告；缺失不能并入零事件。最重要的 Skill 规则是把放置精度、时间稳定性、机械耐久、患者结局四层分开，并让每个几何汇总都保留坐标、标志点、影像、参考时点、随访与分母。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including all six study characteristics and every stability, operation-time, and complication table.
The automatic experimental-mechanical and animal cues are incorrect.
The review is valuable for endpoint taxonomy and missing-harm handling, but not for mechanical reliability or causal superiority.
